svg.text: DOCA-Host components: two ways to sit on a server, and where the compat layer lives

Left: DOCA user space runs over the distro's own (inbox) kernel drivers, with no compat needed. Right: a DOCA-Host profile with a kernel part replaces the inbox RDMA/mlx5 stack, and the compat layer makes that one source build on every distro kernel.
A. DOCA user space over the INBOX kernel
DOCA packages without the kernel part. The kernel's own mlx5 / RDMA modules stay. No compat.
B. Full DOCA-Host profile REPLACES the inbox stack
doca-ofed / doca-roce / doca-host-basic / doca-networking / doca-all: mlnx-ofa_kernel built by DKMS.
rdma-core: libibverbs + libmlx5 (DevX, Direct Verbs), librdmacm
NVIDIA build (or the distro's). Asks the kernel and firmware what is supported (query caps) and turns off what the inbox kernel lacks.
rdma-core: libibverbs + libmlx5 (DevX, Direct Verbs), librdmacm
NVIDIA build (version like 2410mlnx...), matched to the DOCA kernel stack it ships with.
The kernel never breaks it: new user space runs on old kernels and the other way round.
This is why mode A needs no compat: DOCA user space only uses this door.
What it finds behind it (kernel + firmware caps) decides which features work.
Lustre, GPFS, nvidia-peermem: vs distro headers
/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/... built and signed by the distro vendor,
source = upstream mlx5 at the distro's kernel version + what Red Hat / Canonical / SUSE backported
same name, newer code: backport of
so the whole stack is replaced
NVIDIA's own copy of the RDMA subsystem
must be rebuilt vs DOCA headers
/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/updates/dkms/... package mlnx-ofa_kernel, built on the host by DKMS,
signed with a local MOK key. depmod ranks updates/ above kernel/, so modprobe loads these.
The modules were compiled as part of this exact kernel, so every API they call exists.
Cost: features are only what the distro backported. They can lag upstream by months or years.
The inbox files are what mode B hides. They stay on disk untouched (see the grey box on the right).
inbox modules still on disk in kernel/..., shadowed, not loaded
remove the DOCA packages + depmod + rebuild initramfs and they come back
Linux kernel core (RHEL 8 4.18, RHEL 9 5.14, Ubuntu 22.04 5.15 / 24.04 6.8, SLES 15 6.4 ...)
netdev core, page_pool, XDP, PCI, DMA, devlink core, auxiliary bus, IRQ. Same kernel in both modes.
Its internal API is NOT stable and differs on every distro: the compat layer is what lets mode B link to it.
PCIe: physical function (PF) and SR-IOV virtual functions (VF), BAR doorbells, DMA to host memory, MSI-X interrupts. Same in both modes. The device cannot tell which driver is loaded.
No CPU for apps. The host's mlx5 driver is its only control plane.
Firmware is burnt with mlnx-fw-updater / mlxfwmanager (DOCA-Host) or mstflint (inbox).
BlueField DPU (BlueField-2, BlueField-3: needs DOCA-Host, not MLNX_OFED, on the host)
A ConnectX inside, plus its own Arm computer. To the host it looks like a ConnectX (same mlx5 PCI functions).
and RDMA engines as the NIC
In DPU mode the eswitch is
owned by the Arm side, not
switched by OVS on the Arm
Arm subsystem: runs the BFB image (its own OS)
programmable with DOCA (FlexIO / DPA SDK), close to the packets
DOCA Comch / DMA: host DOCA apps talk to DOCA services on the Arm (over PCIe)
Inbox modules on disk, not loaded

Green arrows cross the stable uAPI (both modes). Orange arrows: in mode B the driver reaches the kernel core only through the compat layer. Blue: in mode A the inbox modules call the kernel core directly.
Kubernetes: the NVIDIA Network Operator can do either mode, keeping the inbox driver or loading the DOCA-Host kernel part from a driver container.
